questions.prompt: What is static addressing?
options: Letting a server hand out an address each time
Typing the address into the device by hand
Using only the device's MAC address to talk
Giving every device the same address at once

questions.prompt: Which device should get a static address?
options: A tablet used for a day
A visitor's phone on Wi-Fi
A laptop that comes and goes
A printer others must find

questions.prompt: What is a risk of typing addresses by hand?
options: The device loses its MAC address
The device can never reach a router
A typo can cause an address conflict
The address changes every single day

questions.prompt: What does DHCP stand for?
options: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
Direct Hardware Connection Port
Domain Host Control Program for IPv4
Dynamic Hub Channel Process

questions.prompt: Besides an address, what else can DHCP hand out?
options: The cable and the switch port
The gateway and DNS server
The password for the Wi-Fi
The MAC address of the NIC

questions.prompt: What is a DHCP reservation?
options: A spare DHCP server kept for emergencies
The same address always given to one device
An address that nobody is allowed to use
A lease that never needs to be renewed at all

questions.prompt: What are the four DHCP steps, in order?
options: Request, Offer, Discover, Acknowledge
Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge
Discover, Request, Offer, Acknowledge
Offer, Discover, Acknowledge, Request

questions.prompt: Why is the DHCP Discover a broadcast?
options: The client has no address and knows no server
Broadcasts are faster than any other message
The server only listens to broadcasts on port 80
The client wants every device to get its address

questions.prompt: In DORA, what does the server send in the Offer?
options: A copy of every lease it has given out
An address it will lend, plus settings
A request for the client's MAC address
The client's old address from last time

questions.prompt: Why is the Request step also broadcast?
options: So other servers know their offer lost
So the router can copy the lease for itself
So the DNS server can learn the client's name
So the client can ask for two addresses at once

questions.prompt: Which UDP ports does DHCP use?
options: 20 and 21
53 and 54
67 and 68

questions.prompt: When does a client first try to renew its lease?
options: Only after the lease expires
Halfway through the lease
Only when the user asks it to
Every time it sends a packet

questions.prompt: What is centralized DHCP?
options: One server managing many subnets' pools
One DHCP server inside every single subnet
A DHCP server built into each network card
Every client handing out its own address

questions.prompt: Why can't a client on another subnet reach a central DHCP server on its own?
options: The server only serves one MAC address
The cable is longer than 100 meters
Clients cannot send UDP at all
Routers do not forward broadcasts

questions.prompt: What does a DHCP relay agent do?
options: Forwards the broadcast on as a unicast
Blocks every DHCP message on the router
Hands out addresses without any server at all
Turns IP addresses into names for clients

questions.prompt: On a Cisco router, which command sets up a DHCP relay?
options: ipconfig /renew
ip dhcp relay-on
ip helper-address
route add dhcp-relay

questions.prompt: What is a DHCP scope?
options: The address rules for one subnet
The time a client waits before asking again
The cable range that DHCP messages can reach
The list of every device's MAC address

questions.prompt: A DHCP scope has no default gateway option. What can its clients do?
options: Nothing at all, not even locally
Reach the Internet but not the LAN
Everything, the gateway is optional
Only talk on their own network

questions.prompt: A pool runs from .100 to .150. How many addresses can it hand out?
The pool is exhausted. What happens to the next client?
options: It is given the router's address instead
It takes the address of the oldest client
It gets no offer and has no address
The server makes the pool bigger on its own

questions.prompt: Why keep static devices outside the DHCP pool?
options: So the pool can be made as small as possible
So static devices can reach the Internet
So DHCP never hands out an address in use
So the server does not need a subnet mask

questions.prompt: What does DNS do?

Turns names into IP addresses
Splits a network into subnets
Sends mail between two servers

lan
codexia.lan
portal

options: Names are stored inside each NIC
DNS servers sit on every single LAN
Resolvers cache answers for the TTL
The router remembers every page

AAAA

NS

A reverse lookup from address to name
